title: Rubato Security Against Chosen-Plaintext Attacks
summary: The authors believe Rubato resists the named chosen-plaintext attacks, but the security claim remains unproved and must be proved or refuted.

formal_statement.body: Prove or refute security of Rubato against the stated chosen-plaintext attack classes under the random-oracle XOF model.

scope.domain: This is a cryptanalysis question about the symmetric construction Rubato under chosen-plaintext attacks.
assumptions: The XOF is modeled as a random oracle.
The attack model permits adversarially chosen nonces.
parameters: Chosen-plaintext attack classes: higher-order differential, truncated differential, invariant-subspace trail, and cube attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute Rubato's security against all of the named chosen-plaintext attack classes.

citations.label: Rubato: Noisy Ciphers for Approximate Homomorphic Encryption

progress.summary: The paper attributes its belief to the random-oracle treatment of the XOF and the resulting inability of chosen nonces to control internal differences. It presents security against higher-order and truncated differential, invariant-subspace, and cube attacks as an unproved claim.
citation_labels: Jincheol Ha et al., Rubato: Noisy Ciphers for Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
